title: Adaptive entropy-based sequence bucketing for KV-cache onboarding and deterministic version pin playbook
creator: Ava Patel
description:
Problem:
Customers and internal workloads show widely different long-context distributions. Current onboarding uses coarse heuristics (fixed length buckets and ad-hoc retention) that either over-pin model versions or cause repeated cache churn, leading to latency spikes and higher token cost. We need an onboarding workflow that derives per-model, per-sequence-distribution profiles from traces, groups sequences into entropy-informed buckets, and produces deterministic version-pinning and publishable performance profiles for the console and runtime.

Goal:
1) Automatically produce stable KV-cache retention and prefetch rules per model variant using sequence entropy + length bucketing.
2) Create a deterministic, auditable version-pinning playbook that maps live traffic buckets to a pinned model variant + fallback path.
3) Publish a concise performance profile (latency P50/P95, warmup cost, KV retention ratio) for each pinned variant in the catalog and Console.

Non-goals:
- Replacing runtime cache eviction algorithms (we will generate profiles consumable by runtime but not modify eviction core in this ticket).
- Full rollout of adaptive online re-pin; first iteration is offline profile generation with canary rollout automation later.
acceptance_criteria: Profile generator consumes golden trace set + 72h live-sampled sequences and outputs bucketed profiles with entropy, sequence-length quantiles, and recommended retention/prefetch settings for model variants
Deterministic pin mapping produced as a small immutable manifest for runtime (model_variant_id -> bucket selector -> retention/prefetch parameters)
Console shows published profile for at least two model variants with latency P50/P95 and estimated warmup token cost
End-to-end test: synthetic workload with mixed entropy distributions yields <=10% P95 latency regression compared to baseline on pinned variants and no increased tail error rates
Documentation and playbook published in Confluence and linked from onboarding flow
approach: 1) Define sequence 'entropy' metric (Shannon bits over token distribution per session/segment) and validate correlation with KV-hit rate on historical traces. 2) Run offline clustering combining entropy and length quantiles into 6 buckets (Very Low, Low, Medium, High, Very High, Dynamic). 3) For each model variant, simulate KV retention/prefetch configs across buckets using golden traces to compute warmup token cost and steady-state hit rates. 4) Select deterministic pin candidate (variant + retention) per bucket using a multi-objective score (weighted: latency P95, warmup cost, cost per token). 5) Emit immutable manifest used by runtime routing layer and Console publish API. 6) Provide a rollback safety net by attaching a fallback candidate and a circuit-breaker TTL on pins. 7) Add CI job to validate profile generation vs a baseline sample each night.

Gather telemetry, iterate thresholds, and then schedule broader rollout
monitoring: Per-bucket P50/P95 latency exported to Console (tagged by manifest id)
Warmup token burn rate (tokens/sec) and incremental cost estimate exported per-candidate
KV-hit ratio and eviction churn rate per bucket
tests: Unit: entropy calculation correctness on token streams
Integration: profile generator produces stable manifests given fixed seed traces
E2E: canary tenant traffic with staged pins shows no >15% P95 regression vs unpinned baseline
Chaos: simulate a sudden shift to higher-entropy traffic and verify fallback activation
risks: Entropy metric may not generalize across languages; need language-aware normalization
Overfitting to golden traces could create pins that degrade on real traffic bursts
Manifest size growth if we create too many fine-grained buckets; must cap to 6-8
